# HeyMile

> HeyMile ("HeyMile: Mileage Tracker" on the App Store) is a mileage log for iPhone and CarPlay, made by AGNTPOOL, LLC (Texas, USA) for self-employed people, 1099 contractors and small businesses who drive for work. It detects drives and logs the miles automatically, asks "Business or personal?" on the Lock Screen, in a widget and on CarPlay so each drive is answered with one tap, logs trips by voice or typing with Apple Maps, and exports PDF and spreadsheet reports. No account, no ads, no analytics. Free to download; the HeyMile Monthly subscription is $0.99 a month, with the first month free for new subscribers.

Last updated: 2026-11-21. Current version: 1.0 (first released November 21, 2026).

## Key facts

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/heymile-mileage-tracker/id6834995051 (App Store ID 6834995051). Seller on the App Store: AGNTPOOL LLC. Available on the United States App Store.
- Platform: iPhone with iOS 26 or later, with CarPlay. There is no Android, iPad or web version.
- Languages: English and Spanish (Spanish App Store name: "HeyMile: Registro de millas"). Reports are generated in English.
- Price: HeyMile is a free download. Using it requires the HeyMile Monthly subscription: $0.99 a month, auto-renewing, billed through the Apple Account, with the first month free for new subscribers. After cancelling, people can still read and export their records.
- Account: HeyMile needs no account, sign-up, email address or password. The subscription is handled by the person's Apple Account.
- Required setup for automatic tracking: location access for HeyMile must be set to Always (iPhone Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location > Always, with Precise Location on), and tracking must be turned on in the app (the top of HeyMile's first screen says "Tracking on"). When tracking is turned on, iOS first asks to allow location access, then to "Change to Always Allow". With "While Using the App" only, HeyMile cannot log drives on its own. Without location access, trips can still be logged by voice or typing.
- Automatic tracking: HeyMile detects drives and logs the miles even when the app is closed; it can also start a drive when the car connects. A drive is kept only if it is longer than 0.2 miles and one minute. A Drive control (Control Center, Lock Screen, Action button) starts or ends a drive by hand.
- Battery: between drives HeyMile relies on low-power signals from iOS; precise GPS runs only while a drive is being recorded.
- One tap, business or personal: when a drive ends, the Lock Screen (Live Activity), a Home Screen widget and CarPlay ask "Business or personal?". A business drive then gets its purpose, which is asked on the iPhone.
- CarPlay is optional: HeyMile works on the iPhone alone, where the Lock Screen and the Home Screen widget ask "Business or personal?" after each drive with one tap. People without CarPlay get the same automatic logging and one-tap answers.
- CarPlay: while driving, the car's screen shows the miles so far (for example "Driving · 2.4 mi") with two large buttons, Business (blue briefcase) and Personal (green house). After the drive it shows, for example, "Last drive: 22.8 mi" with the same buttons. The purpose of a business drive is never asked in the car.
- Works alongside other apps: HeyMile does not connect to, sign in to, or read data from rideshare, delivery or booking apps. It logs the drives the iPhone detects, so miles from several apps end up in one log.
- Voice and typing: "From the office to 1200 Main St" logs a trip measured with Apple Maps; place names are looked up in Apple Maps. Questions like "How many miles this month?" and edits like "Make Monday's trip personal" work too. HeyMile asks before it adds, changes or deletes anything. On iPhones with Apple Intelligence, requests are understood by Apple's on-device model, which can only read the log; on other iPhones the same example requests work through HeyMile's own rules. Spotlight can find any trip by place or purpose.
- Reports: PDF or spreadsheet for a month or a year, with each trip's date, route, purpose and miles, plus odometer readings. Dollar figures are estimates using the IRS standard mileage rate for the day each trip was driven. HeyMile starts with the rates in effect from July 1, 2026 (76 cents a mile for business), and trips can't be dated before July 1, 2026.
- Map: every trip on one map, business in blue and personal in green.
- Privacy: no account, no ads, no analytics. The log stays on the iPhone and in the person's own iCloud; the developer never sees trips, locations or voice.
- What HeyMile isn't: not tax advice (it is a record-keeping tool; its estimates aren't guaranteed; confirm with a tax advisor before filing); not a team or fleet dashboard (each driver uses HeyMile on their own iPhone with their own log); not connected to any gig or delivery app.
- Developer: AGNTPOOL, LLC (Texas, USA). Support: support@heymile.app

## Home page questions

Q: How much does HeyMile cost?
A: $0.99 a month, and the first month is free for new subscribers. It renews each month until you cancel, billed through your Apple Account. If you cancel, you can still read and export your records.

Q: Does HeyMile log drives automatically?
A: Yes, once two things are on: location access set to Always, and tracking turned on. Then HeyMile detects your drives and logs the miles, even when the app is closed. You can also have every drive start when your car connects. When you arrive, the Lock Screen asks “Business or personal?” and one tap answers.

Q: What do I need to turn on?
A: In the iPhone’s Settings, tap Apps, then HeyMile, then Location, and choose Always, with Precise Location on. When you turn tracking on, iOS asks twice: allow location access, then choose Change to Always Allow. With While Using the App only, HeyMile can’t log drives on its own. Then check the top of HeyMile’s first screen: it should say Tracking on. If it says anything else, tap it.

Q: Does HeyMile work with CarPlay?
A: Yes. On the car’s screen HeyMile shows the drive with two big buttons, Business and Personal, so you can answer with one tap before you leave the car.

Q: Do I need CarPlay to use HeyMile?
A: No. CarPlay is optional. Without it, the iPhone’s Lock Screen and the Home Screen widget ask “Business or personal?” after each drive, and one tap answers. CarPlay adds two big buttons on the car’s screen.

Q: What is in the report?
A: Every trip with its date, route, purpose and miles, and your odometer readings, exported as a PDF or a spreadsheet for the month or the year.

Q: Do I need an account?
A: No. HeyMile has no account, no ads and no analytics. Your log lives on your iPhone and in your own iCloud.

Q: Which iPhones does HeyMile run on?
A: iPhone with iOS 26 or later, in English or Spanish.

Q: Is HeyMile free?
A: HeyMile is free to download. Using it requires the HeyMile Monthly subscription: $0.99 a month, with the first month free for new subscribers.

Q: Does HeyMile work if I drive for more than one app?
A: Yes. HeyMile doesn’t connect to rideshare, delivery or booking apps. It logs the drives your iPhone detects, so miles from every app you drive for end up in one log.

Q: Does HeyMile drain my battery?
A: Between drives HeyMile relies on low-power signals from iOS. Precise GPS runs only while a drive is being recorded.

Q: Does HeyMile work on Android?
A: No. HeyMile is an iPhone app, for iOS 26 or later, and it isn’t available for Android, iPad or the web.

Q: Is HeyMile tax advice?
A: No. HeyMile is a record-keeping tool. Dollar figures are estimates based on your log and the IRS standard mileage rate and aren’t guaranteed. Confirm with your tax advisor before you file.

## Guide: IRS standard mileage rates for 2026
Page: https://heymile.app/irs-mileage-rate/

Checked against irs.gov on November 21, 2026. General information from IRS publications, not tax advice. HeyMile is not affiliated with or endorsed by the IRS.

For 2026 the IRS set two business rates: 72.5 cents a mile for drives from January 1 to June 30, and 76 cents a mile for drives from July 1 to December 31.

### The rates

IRS standard mileage rates, in cents per mile
    Period | Business | Medical or military moving | Charity

      July 1 – Dec. 31, 2026 | 76 | 23.5 | 14

      Jan. 1 – June 30, 2026 | 72.5 | 20.5 | 14

      2025 | 70 | 21 | 14

  Source: IRS standard mileage rates (https://www.irs.gov/tax-professionals/standard-mileage-rates) on irs.gov. The moving rate applies to members of the military only.

### Why 2026 has two business rates

In Announcement 2026-11 (https://www.irs.gov/irb/2026-29_irb), the IRS raised the business rate from 72.5 to 76 cents and the medical and moving rate from 20.5 to 23.5 cents, for drives on or after July 1, 2026. The IRS said the change results from recent increases in the price of fuel. Drives before July 1 keep the earlier 2026 rates.

The charity rate stays at 14 cents a mile, because it is fixed in the tax code rather than set by the IRS each year.

### Standard rate or actual expenses

The standard rate is one of two ways to work out car costs for business. The other is actual expenses: the business share of what you spend on gas, oil, repairs, tires, insurance, registration, licenses and depreciation or lease payments. Topic 510, Business use of car (https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc510) explains both.

A few rules from Topic 510 are worth knowing before you choose:
  
     - For a car you own, you must choose the standard rate in the first year the car is available for use in your business. In later years you can choose either method.
     - For a leased car, if you choose the standard rate you use it for the entire lease period.
     - You can’t use the standard rate if you operate five or more cars at the same time, as in a fleet.
     - Parking fees and tolls for business use can be deducted separately under either method.
  
  Which method fits you is a question for your tax advisor. Either way, you need a record of your business miles.

### How HeyMile uses the rate

HeyMile shows estimates, such as an estimated deduction for the month, by multiplying the miles in your log by the IRS standard rate for the day each trip was driven. It starts with the rates in effect from July 1, 2026, so trips in HeyMile can’t be dated before July 1, 2026. When the IRS sets a new rate, an app update adds it, and each trip keeps the rate of the day it was driven.

The estimates aren’t guaranteed, and HeyMile isn’t tax advice.

### The 2027 rate

As of November 21, 2026, the IRS has not announced the standard mileage rates for 2027. The IRS usually announces the next year’s rates near the end of the year. This page will be updated when it does.

Q: What is the IRS mileage rate for 2026?
A: 72.5 cents a mile for business drives from January 1 to June 30, 2026, and 76 cents a mile for business drives from July 1 to December 31, 2026.

Q: What are the 2026 medical and moving rates?
A: 20.5 cents a mile through June 30, 2026, and 23.5 cents a mile from July 1, 2026. The moving rate is for members of the military only.

Q: What is the 2026 charity mileage rate?
A: 14 cents a mile for the whole year. It is fixed in the tax code.

Q: Has the IRS announced the 2027 mileage rate?
A: Not as of November 21, 2026. This page will be updated when it is announced.

## Guide: What a mileage log should include, according to the IRS
Page: https://heymile.app/mileage-log-requirements/

Checked against irs.gov on November 21, 2026. General information from IRS publications, not tax advice. HeyMile is not affiliated with or endorsed by the IRS. Based on the edition of Publication 463 for 2025 returns.

IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463) lists what your records should show for each business use of a car, and when to write it down. Here is a plain-language summary, with links to the source.

### What each business drive should show

For car expenses, Publication 463 asks for:
  
     - The date of each business use of the car.
     - Your business destination.
     - The business purpose of the drive.
     - The mileage for each business use.
     - The total miles you drove the car during the year.
  
  If you deduct actual expenses instead of using the standard rate, your records also need the cost of the car and any improvements, the date you started using it for business, and the cost of each expense.

### Write it down at or near the time

Publication 463 says to record each business use at or near the time it happens, because a record kept at the time has more value than one prepared later from memory. You don’t have to write everything down the same day: a log kept weekly that accounts for the week’s driving counts as a timely kept record.

### Paper, spreadsheet or app

Publication 463 lists an account book, diary, log, statement of expense, trip sheets or a similar record as ways to keep proof, and says a record prepared on a computer is considered an adequate record. What matters is that it has the details above and was kept at the time.

To keep one by hand, start with our mileage log template (/mileage-log-template.csv) (a spreadsheet file with one column for each detail).

### How long to keep it

Generally, keep the records that support a deduction for 3 years from the date you file the return that claims it. Publication 463 and Publication 583 explain the exceptions.

### Commuting isn’t business driving

Publication 463 says you can’t deduct commuting between your home and your main or regular place of work, no matter how far it is. Drives between work locations, to a temporary work location, or from a home office that is your principal place of business can be different. These rules depend on your situation, so a complete log of every drive, sorted business and personal, lets your tax advisor apply them to the facts.

### Schedule C asks about written evidence

If you file Schedule C, Part IV asks whether you have evidence to support your car deduction and whether that evidence is written. The Schedule C instructions (https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1040sc) point to Publication 463 for the record-keeping rules.

### What HeyMile records

HeyMile keeps the log as you drive. For each trip it records the date and time, where the drive started and ended, the miles, whether it was business or personal and, for a business drive, the purpose you give it. Reports, as a PDF or a spreadsheet for the month or the year, list each trip’s date, route, purpose and miles, with your odometer readings.

Automatic logging needs two settings: location access for HeyMile set to Always, and tracking turned on in the app. HeyMile is a record-keeping tool, not tax advice.

Q: What does the IRS require in a mileage log?
A: For each business use of a car: the date, the business destination, the business purpose and the miles, plus the total miles for the year. See IRS Publication 463.

Q: Does a mileage log have to be on paper?
A: No. Publication 463 says a record prepared on a computer is considered an adequate record.

Q: How often should I update my mileage log?
A: At or near the time of each drive. A log kept weekly that accounts for the week’s use is considered a timely kept record.

Q: How long should I keep my mileage log?
A: Generally 3 years from the date you file the return that claims the deduction. Publication 463 and Publication 583 explain the exceptions.

## Guide: A mileage log on your car’s screen
Page: https://heymile.app/carplay-mileage-tracker/

HeyMile works with Apple CarPlay. The car’s screen shows the drive’s miles with two big buttons, Business and Personal. One tap answers the drive, when it’s safe or once you park.

### While you drive

The car’s screen shows “Driving” and the miles so far, updated at most every 10 seconds, with two large buttons below: Business, a blue briefcase, and Personal, a green house. When it’s safe, or once you park, tap one and the title shows your answer. Tap the other to change it. There is nothing to type and no list to scroll.

### When you park

If the drive wasn’t answered on the way, the car’s screen shows the last drive, such as “Last drive: 22.8 mi”, with the same two buttons, so you can answer before you leave the car. The same question waits on your iPhone’s Lock Screen and in the widget.

### The purpose is asked on your iPhone

What a business drive was for is never asked in the car. HeyMile asks on your iPhone: on the Lock Screen card, in a notification, or the next time you open the app.

### Start every drive when your car connects

Besides detecting drives on its own, HeyMile can start a drive the moment your car connects, so each drive is caught from the start. Set it up by tapping the tracking status at the top of HeyMile’s first screen.

### Set it up

- In the iPhone’s Settings, tap Apps, then HeyMile, then Location, and choose Always, with Precise Location on.
     - Check that the top of HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.
     - For the question to appear on the car’s screen when you park, turn on Show in CarPlay in the iPhone’s Settings, under Notifications, then HeyMile.
  
  HeyMile then appears on your car’s screen with your other CarPlay apps.

Q: Does HeyMile need CarPlay?
A: No. HeyMile works on the iPhone alone: the Lock Screen and the widget ask the same question. CarPlay adds the two buttons on the car’s screen.

Q: Do I type anything in the car?
A: No. On CarPlay you only tap Business or Personal. The purpose of a business drive is asked on your iPhone, never in the car.

Q: How do I get the question on my car’s screen after I park?
A: Turn on Show in CarPlay in the iPhone’s Settings, under Notifications, then HeyMile.

## Rideshare drivers
Page: https://heymile.app/for/rideshare-drivers/

To the pickup, the ride, back toward the busy part of town, the long drive home from the airport. Your miles add up all shift. HeyMile logs your drives on its own, and you sort each one with a tap on CarPlay or the Lock Screen.

### How a rideshare shift adds up

A shift is dozens of short drives: to the pickup, the ride itself, then repositioning toward the next busy area, or the empty drive back from a far-off drop-off. Many drivers run more than one app at a time, so no single company sees the whole shift.

The summary a rideshare company sends at tax time is its record of your work on its platform, counted its way. It won’t include miles you drove for other apps, and it may not match every mile you drove for work. Your own log fills that gap.

### Why your own log matters

The IRS asks for records that show, for each business drive, the date, where you went, the business purpose and the miles, kept at or near the time of the drive. IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463) explains what counts as an adequate record. Schedule C also asks whether you have written evidence for the vehicle miles you claim.

Which rideshare miles count, such as the drive from home to your first pickup, depends on your situation. A complete log lets you and your tax advisor make that call with the facts in front of you.

### How HeyMile helps

- Every drive, logged on its own. HeyMile detects your drives and logs the miles, even with the app closed. Set it to start a drive when your car connects, so drives are caught from the start.
- Answer on CarPlay. Two big buttons on the car’s screen: Business and Personal. Tap one when you’re stopped at the curb between rides. There’s nothing to type.
- Or on the Lock Screen. When a drive ends, the Lock Screen asks “Business or personal?” One tap, and you’re back in the rideshare app.
- Add a missed drive by voice. Say “From the airport to downtown” and HeyMile measures the route with Apple Maps, then asks before it logs anything.
- Reports when you need them. Export the month or the year as a PDF or a spreadsheet, with each trip’s date, route, purpose and miles, and your odometer readings.

Before the first drive: set HeyMile’s location access to Always (Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location), with Precise Location on, and check that HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.

### Questions

Q: Does HeyMile connect to my rideshare app?
A: No. HeyMile doesn’t sign in to any other app or read your earnings. It logs the drives your iPhone detects, and you decide which ones were business.

Q: I drive for more than one app. Do I need more than one log?
A: No. HeyMile logs the drive, not the app, so the miles from every platform you drive for end up in one log and one report.

Q: Do I have to answer after every ride?
A: HeyMile asks once for each drive it logs, on the Lock Screen, in the widget or on CarPlay. If you’re busy, answer later: open HeyMile, or tell it something like “Mark the trip to Main St as business”.

## Food and grocery delivery
Page: https://heymile.app/for/delivery-drivers/

Restaurant, customer, back to the busy zone, again. Delivery work is many short drives, and HeyMile records each one so you don’t have to remember them at tax time.

### What a delivery shift looks like

Food and grocery delivery means short hops between restaurants, stores and doorsteps, waiting in parking lots, and driving back toward busier areas between orders. A single evening can be twenty drives or more, and a weekend can mix delivery runs with your own errands in the same car.

Few people write down twenty drives a night by hand. Rebuilding them months later from memory and order history is slow, and it leaves gaps.

### Why a log made as you drive matters

A mileage log is most useful when it’s made as you go. The IRS describes adequate records as ones made at or near the time of the drive, showing the date, the place, the business purpose and the miles (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)). A delivery app’s summary covers only its own orders, counted its own way.

Mixed days are where a log earns its keep: the drive to the store for an order is business, the stop for your own groceries isn’t. One tap at the end of each drive keeps them apart.

### How HeyMile helps

- Logs in the background. HeyMile detects drives even when it’s closed, so your delivery app can stay on screen.
- Business or Personal on CarPlay. Two big buttons on the car’s screen answer each drive with one tap, before you head to the door.
- A widget that asks for you. On the Home Screen, the widget shows your miles this year and, when a drive is waiting, Business and Personal in one tap.
- Start a drive yourself. Add the Drive control to Control Center or the Action button to start or end a drive with one press.
- One report for every app. Export the month or the year as a PDF or a spreadsheet, with business and personal miles kept apart.

Before the first drive: set HeyMile’s location access to Always (Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location), with Precise Location on, and check that HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.

### Questions

Q: Will HeyMile keep logging while my delivery app is open?
A: Yes. HeyMile detects drives in the background, even when it’s closed, so your delivery app can stay on screen.

Q: I deliver for several apps. Do I need separate logs?
A: No. HeyMile logs your drives, whichever app sent you, so all your delivery miles are in one log and one report.

Q: Can I keep my own errands out of it?
A: Yes. Every drive is Business or Personal. Personal drives stay in your log, but reports list them apart from your business miles.

## Real estate agents
Page: https://heymile.app/for/real-estate-agents/

Showings, listing appointments, open houses, inspections, closings. HeyMile logs the drives between them and keeps the purpose with each one.

### Where an agent’s miles go

An agent’s week is drives to properties and clients: showings across town, listing presentations, open houses, inspections and appraisals, the title office, and back to the brokerage. Many agents work as independent contractors and drive their own car, so those miles are a cost of their business.

No two days repeat. One day is three showings in one neighborhood, the next is a listing appointment forty minutes out, which makes a weekly estimate a poor stand-in for a real log.

### Why the purpose matters

The IRS expects each business drive in your records to show its business purpose, along with the date, the place and the miles (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)). For an agent, “Showing, 412 Elm St” or “Listing appointment” is the line that ties a drive to your work. Write it at the time, and the log explains itself later.

### How HeyMile helps

- Business, then the purpose. Tap Business on the Lock Screen and HeyMile asks what the drive was for. One answer, saved with the trip.
- Log by place name. Say “From the office to 412 Elm St”: HeyMile finds the address in Apple Maps, asks if it’s the right one, and measures the miles.
- Find any trip in Spotlight. Search by place or purpose, such as a street name, to pull up every drive to it.
- CarPlay between appointments. Business or Personal in one tap on the car’s screen, before you walk into the next showing.
- Reports by month or year. A PDF or a spreadsheet with each trip’s date, route, purpose and miles, to share with your tax advisor.

Before the first drive: set HeyMile’s location access to Always (Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location), with Precise Location on, and check that HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.

### Questions

Q: Do I need CarPlay to use HeyMile?
A: No. CarPlay is optional. Without it, the Lock Screen and the Home Screen widget ask “Business or personal?” after each drive, and one tap answers. CarPlay adds two big buttons on the car’s screen.

Q: Can I record which property or client a drive was for?
A: Yes. Each business drive has a purpose, and you write whatever helps you, such as the address or the kind of appointment. HeyMile can also offer to add the client’s name.

Q: My brokerage asks for mileage. Can I send them a report?
A: Yes. Export a PDF or a spreadsheet for the month or the year and share it from your iPhone. Nothing is sent unless you send it.

Q: What if I forget to start HeyMile before a showing?
A: You don’t need to start it: HeyMile detects drives on its own. If a drive was missed, tell HeyMile where you drove, and it adds it after you confirm.

## Contractors and the trades
Page: https://heymile.app/for/contractors/

Job sites, estimates, the supply house, the next call. If you’re a plumber, electrician, HVAC tech, handyman or general contractor working for yourself, HeyMile logs the drives so you can focus on the work.

### A day of drives between jobs

A service day rarely goes from one address to another and home. There’s the estimate in the morning, the supply-house run for a part, the job, a second trip back for something you didn’t have, then an emergency call across town. Each of those is a drive, and many of them are part of running your business.

Most trucks and vans in the trades also get used for personal driving now and then, which is why keeping business and personal apart matters.

### Why the record matters

A vehicle is one of the bigger costs of running a trade business. Whether you and your tax advisor use the standard mileage rate or actual expenses, the IRS expects records of business use: the date, place, purpose and miles of each business drive, kept at or near the time (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)).

A log built as you go is far easier to keep accurate than one rebuilt from invoices at the end of the year.

### How HeyMile helps

- Starts with the truck. Set HeyMile to start a drive when your vehicle connects to your iPhone, or let it detect drives on its own.
- Big buttons on CarPlay. Business and Personal fill the car’s screen, so one tap answers the drive before you climb out.
- Name the job. After you tap Business, give the purpose in a few words, like “Supply run, Smith job”, so the report reads clearly.
- Fix it by voice. Say “From the shop to 1200 Main St” to add a missed drive, or “Make Monday’s trip personal” to fix one. HeyMile asks before it changes anything.
- A report to share. PDF or spreadsheet, month or year, with odometer readings.

Before the first drive: set HeyMile’s location access to Always (Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location), with Precise Location on, and check that HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.

### Questions

Q: Can I log a drive after the fact?
A: Yes. Tell HeyMile where you drove, and it measures the miles with Apple Maps and asks you to confirm. You can also edit any trip from Trips.

Q: Is the purpose required?
A: No, but HeyMile asks for one on each business drive, because records usually need one. A few words are enough.

Q: Will my crew’s drives be logged too?
A: HeyMile logs the drives of the iPhone it’s on. Each person who drives for your business uses HeyMile on their own iPhone, with their own log.

## Home health and home care
Page: https://heymile.app/for/home-health-care/

Visit to visit, all day. Whether you’re a home health nurse, a therapist, an aide or an independent caregiver, HeyMile logs the drives between homes and keeps the log private.

### Driving is part of the job

Home visits mean driving between clients’ homes, to the pharmacy or the office, and sometimes back to the same home twice in one day. Routes change with the schedule, and the drives can take as much time as the visits.

### A log for reimbursement or for taxes

If you work for an agency that reimburses mileage, it will usually want a log with dates, places and miles before it pays. If you’re an independent contractor or run your own care business, business miles may be deductible, and the IRS expects a record made at or near the time of each drive, with its business purpose (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)). Either way, the record has to exist.

Follow your agency’s rules on what goes in a mileage log. Many prefer a general purpose like “Client visit” rather than names or health details.

### How HeyMile helps

- One tap between visits. When you park, the Lock Screen asks “Business or personal?” Answer before you walk in.
- No starting and stopping. HeyMile detects drives on its own and logs the miles, even with the app closed.
- Private by design. No account, no ads, no analytics. Your log lives on your iPhone and in your own iCloud, and we never see your trips or where you went.
- Reports to send. Export the month as a PDF or a spreadsheet for your agency or your tax advisor.
- In English or Spanish. HeyMile follows your iPhone’s language, typed or spoken.

Before the first drive: set HeyMile’s location access to Always (Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location), with Precise Location on, and check that HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.

### Questions

Q: Does HeyMile store client information?
A: HeyMile stores each trip’s start and end addresses and whatever you type, such as the purpose. All of it stays on your iPhone and in your own iCloud; we never see it. Keep purposes general if your agency asks you to.

Q: Can I send my agency a monthly mileage report?
A: Yes. Open Reports, choose the month, and share the PDF or spreadsheet from your iPhone.

Q: Does HeyMile work in Spanish?
A: Yes. To use Spanish for HeyMile only, open the iPhone’s Settings, then Apps, HeyMile, Language.

### Life in a territory

Outside sales means driving a territory: scheduled calls, drop-in visits, sample deliveries, a trade show two cities over. Some reps are independent, paid on commission and responsible for their own costs. Others are employees reimbursed by the mile.

### Reimbursed or self-employed, the log comes first

Companies that reimburse mileage usually ask for each trip’s date, destination, purpose and miles. Independent reps who deduct business miles need the same details in their records, kept at or near the time (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)).

A log rebuilt at the end of the month from your calendar tends to miss the unplanned stops. A log made as you drive doesn’t.

### How HeyMile helps

- Logs every call. HeyMile detects drives and logs the miles, so the visit you added at the last minute is there too.

- Ask your log. “How many miles this month?” or “What trips did I take Monday?” HeyMile answers from your log.

Q: Can I see how many miles I drove this month?

Q: Does my company see my log?
A: No. HeyMile has no account, and nothing is shared unless you export a report and send it yourself.

Because the schedule is irregular and work days often fall on weekends, it’s easy to forget which drives were for work by the time you sit down with your books.

### Write it down when it happens

The IRS describes good records as ones made at or near the time of the drive, with the date, destination, business purpose and miles (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)). For a creative business, the purpose is often what makes a drive clearly business: “Venue walkthrough for the June wedding.”

### How HeyMile helps

- Find every trip to a venue. Search Spotlight by place or purpose.
- See the year. Every trip on one map, business in blue and personal in green, and a report as a PDF or a spreadsheet.

Page: https://heymile.app/for/couriers/

Lab pickups, legal filings, parcels, same-day runs for local businesses. If you’re a courier driving your own vehicle as a contractor, HeyMile logs the miles while you work.

### Long days, many clients

Independent couriers often work for several dispatchers or brokers, or directly for local businesses: a lab pickup in the morning, a court filing at noon, a parcel route in the afternoon. The days are long, and the paperwork comes from many places, each covering only its own jobs.

### One log for all of it

As a contractor using your own vehicle, your mileage log is your record, not any one client’s. The IRS expects it to show each business drive’s date, destination, purpose and miles, kept at or near the time (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)), and Schedule C asks whether you have written evidence for the miles you claim.

A single log across every client is simpler to keep, and simpler to hand to your tax advisor.

### How HeyMile helps

- Long days, logged. HeyMile detects your drives and logs the miles, even with the app closed.

- Ask your log. “How many miles this month?” HeyMile answers from your log.
- Monthly reports. Export a PDF or a spreadsheet and see every trip of the year on one map.

Before the first drive: set HeyMile’s location access to Always (Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location), with Precise Location on, and check that HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.

### Questions

Q: Can I keep one log for every client I drive for?
A: Yes. HeyMile logs your drives, not your clients’ jobs, so every run goes into one log. The purpose of each drive can name the client.

Q: What if my phone missed a drive?
A: Tell HeyMile where you drove, for example “From the lab to 400 Oak Ave”. It measures the miles with Apple Maps and asks you to confirm.

Q: Can I get a report for just one month?
A: Yes. In Reports, choose the month or the year, then view or share the PDF or spreadsheet.

## Pet sitters and dog walkers
Page: https://heymile.app/for/pet-sitters/

A midday walk, a drop-in visit, an overnight stay, a run to the pet supply store. Your day is short drives between clients’ homes, and HeyMile logs them.

### Short drives, all day

Pet care runs on routes: morning visits, midday walks, evening feedings, and overnight stays, often seven days a week. Each visit is a short drive, and short drives are the ones nobody remembers to write down.

Many pet sitters work on their own or through booking apps, and some take clients both ways. Either way, the miles are yours to keep track of.

### Why a log made at the time helps

The IRS expects a record of each business drive, with its date, destination, purpose and miles, kept at or near the time (IRS Publication 463 (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p463)). A handful of two-mile drives a day adds up over a year, and a log kept as you go is far easier than rebuilding it from your booking history.

### How HeyMile helps

- Every visit, logged. HeyMile detects drives and logs the miles, even with the app closed.
- One tap at the curb. When you park, the Lock Screen asks “Business or personal?” Answer before you get the leash.
- A widget that asks for you. On the Home Screen, the widget shows Business and Personal when a drive is waiting.
- Ask your log. “How many miles this month?” HeyMile answers from your log.
- One report. A PDF or a spreadsheet for the month or the year, with the drives for every client and booking app in one log.

Before the first drive: set HeyMile’s location access to Always (Settings > Apps > HeyMile > Location), with Precise Location on, and check that HeyMile’s first screen says Tracking on.

### Questions

Q: I use a booking app for some clients. Does HeyMile connect to it?
A: No. HeyMile doesn’t connect to other apps. It logs the drives your iPhone detects, whoever booked the visit.

Q: Will HeyMile catch very short drives?
A: A drive is kept when it is longer than 0.2 miles and one minute. You can add any drive it missed by telling HeyMile where you drove.

Q: Can I mark a stop for my own errands as personal?
A: Yes. Every drive is Business or Personal, and reports keep them apart.

HeyMile is a record-keeping tool. Dollar figures in HeyMile are estimates based on the user’s log and the IRS standard mileage rate, and they aren’t guaranteed. HeyMile isn’t tax advice; confirm with a tax advisor before filing.
